## Ownership Rules

- Keep this boundary small, typed, and reusable. Do not import app-specific UI, env, or routing from shared packages.
- Public exports must be intentional and documented in the local `src/index.ts` where present.
- Shared API/domain types belong in the owning domain package or Dart model package, not app pages. `packages/typescript/api-types` is a compatibility aggregate.
- Shared UI must support light/dark themes, keyboard focus, disabled state, loading state, and error state.
- Shared payment/auth utilities must not log secrets or expose provider details to the client.

## Dependency Rules

- Dependencies must flow from runtimes into shared packages, never from packages back into runtime source.
- Package-to-package dependencies must follow the layer rules enforced by `scripts/validators/dependency-graph-validator.mjs`.
- Dart `core` is the foundation layer; Dart services may depend on core/models but not UI kit.
- TypeScript shared packages must avoid service, app, infrastructure, and generated artifact imports.

## Runtime Authority

- Runtime manifests in `apps/*/runtime.manifest.json` and `services/*/runtime.manifest.json` define where this package may be consumed.

## Migration Notes

- Extract reusable contracts and pure domain rules into the owning package before reuse by apps or services.
